articles.author: lynett.eth
articles.description:
Hi, I'm Lyn! I'm the sales lead at Altivox Networks, a cloud compute company with a presence in Springfield, MA. We are at a state of war with all expensive compute.
I may be a sales lead, but I am also a programmer (a pretty bad one). My only experience with compiling to WebAssembly before this was playing around with Hyperware, so I thought, "why not try it out?"
Recently, I came across wasmtime, a fast and secure runtime for WebAssembly on the server, which sent me down on a path of researching about WebAssembly.
If WASM+WASI existed in 2008, we wouldn't have needed to create Docker. That's how important it is. WebAssembly on the server is the future of computing. -Solomon Hykes
We'll be running these benchmarks inside a VM on my server running Proxmox, which should have similar CPU performance to Altivox's Budget VPS line.
OS: Ubuntu 22.04
CPU: 4x Intel Xeon E5-2660v3
RAM: 32GB DDR4-2133
This benchmark will be using Docker version 28.1.1, build 4eba377. Docker has support for wasm through the wasmedge runtime!
We'll be benchmarking three different environments: Docker, Docker + wasmedge, and wasmedge standalone.
There will be three benchmark programs:
calculating 314 million digits of pi
hello world HTTP
echoing WebSockets
articles.title: Benchmarking WASM & Docker

articles.author: DevOps Fundamental
articles.description:
Ethernet: The Foundation of Modern Networks


A few years back, a seemingly innocuous firmware update on a stack of distribution switches in our primary data center brought the entire east coast operations to a grinding halt. The root cause? A subtle MTU mismatch introduced by the update, causing fragmentation and subsequent packet loss on inter-VPC peering connections. The incident highlighted a brutal truth: even in a world of SDN, Kubernetes, and cloud-native architectures, a deep understanding of Ethernet remains paramount. It wasn’t a complex routing protocol failure or a cloud provider outage; it was a fundamental layer-2 issue that cascaded into a layer-3 disaster. This incident, and countless others, underscore why mastering Ethernet isn’t just about passing a certification exam – …
articles.title: Networking Fundamentals: Ethernet

articles.author: Bishal Shrestha
articles.description:
I recently published @bishal-shrestha/rest-client, a minimal and efficient REST client for JavaScript and TypeScript developers. It is designed to simplify API communication while remaining fully customizable and environment-agnostic.
Full TypeScript support with rich typings
Works in both Node.js and browser environments
Supports request and response interceptors
Built-in error handling and retry logic
ESM, UMD and CommonJS compatible
Lightweight and dependency-free
npm install @bishal-shrestha/rest-client

import RestClient from '@bishal-shrestha/rest-client';
const api = new RestClient('https://api.example.com');
const user = await api.getAsync('users/1');
console.log(user);

You can also set headers, intercept requests or responses, and customize error handling and retries.
Comprehensive documentation is available at
https://rest-client-docs.netlify.app
The documentation site is built with Docusaurus and deployed via Netlify. Contributions to documentation and examples are welcome.
This project is actively maintained and open to feedback, feature suggestions, and contributions. If you find the client useful, consider contributing by:
Reporting issues or bugs
Suggesting or implementing features
Helping improve documentation
Providing use case feedback
Let me know your thoughts or suggestions. I’m open to collaboration and always looking to improve the library based on real-world use.
articles.title: A Modern, Typed REST Client for Node.js and Browsers

Whether you're a newbie, a frontend developer trying to improve your skills, or someone interested in full-stack development, here are some frontend technologies that are currently in demand and will likely remain so in the future.

Massive community and job market.
Backed by huge technology.
Endless ecosystem (e.g., Next.js, Redux, TanStack).

Used in practically all professional code bases.
Improves the maintainability of large projects.
Most frontend job advertisements require this.

Why is it here to stay?
Clean and reusable code
Easy to theme and extend.
Widely used by startups and enterprise organizations.

Tool: Why It Matters
Vite offers lightning-fast development servers and bundlers.
ESLint + Prettier Clean, readable code is generated automatically.
Storybook Component documentation and testing.
Playwright and Cypress provide end-to-end testing frameworks.

Final Thoughts -
The optimal technology stack is one that solves real-world challenges and helps you advance as a developer.
So, if you want to advance your career in technology, start with React, learn TypeScript, and confidently style with Tailwind CSS. Explore technologies like Next.js, Vite, and testing frameworks to round out your toolkit.
